bib.title: Bandit Algorithms, Chapter 11: The Exp3 Algorithm

question: Can a randomised policy achieve sublinear worst-case regret against an arbitrary (adversarial) reward sequence with bandit feedback, and how does Exp3 do it?
contributions: Formal model of k-armed adversarial bandits and expected regret against best fixed arm
Exp3 algorithm (Algorithm 9) and regret bounds 2sqrt(nk log k) and sqrt(2nk log k)

limits: Horizon n must be known to set eta (Note 10: doubling trick or decreasing rate).
Expected regret is near-optimal but its distribution is not: constant probability of linear regret (Note 1, Ex 11.6); fixed in next chapter.
Bound is suboptimal by sqrt(log k) (Note 5).
Regret vs best fixed arm has stationarity built in; poor fit for non-stationary bandits (Note 8).
Rewards must be bounded in [0,1]; unbounded case only weak results (Note 2).
No sublinear policy regret for reactive adversaries without limited-memory assumptions (Note 7).
Chapter has no benchmark experiments beyond two exercise plots.
practices: Use the loss-based estimator 1-I{A_t=i}(1-X_t)/P_ti in Exp3, because it is bounded above by 1, which the exp(x)<=1+x+x^2 argument needs (Sec 11.4).
Set eta=sqrt(2 log(k)/(nk)) (Thm 11.2) rather than sqrt(log(k)/(nk)) for the tighter bound.
Initial distribution P_1 need not be uniform; biasing toward a likely-best arm cuts regret if right, costs if wrong (Note 6).
Use randomised policies; deterministic ones (UCB, ETC) have linear adversarial regret (Sec 11.1).
Check reduction assumptions (bounded support) before using adversarial algorithms on stochastic problems (Note 11).

terms.definition: A k-armed adversarial bandit is an arbitrary sequence of reward vectors (x_t), x_t in [0,1]^k.
R_n(pi,x) = max_i sum_t x_ti - E[sum_t x_tA_t]: expected loss in revenue relative to the best fixed action in hindsight.
X_hat_ti = I{A_t=i} X_t / P_ti, unbiased for x_ti given the past; loss-based variant X_hat_ti = 1 - I{A_t=i}(1-X_t)/P_ti.
exponential-weight algorithm for exploration and exploitation: P_ti proportional to exp(eta * S_hat_{t-1,i}) with S_hat the cumulative importance-weighted reward estimate.
Large eta concentrates P_t on the arm with largest estimated reward (exploits); small eta makes P_t more uniform (explores).
Adversary that chooses all rewards at the start; reactive adversary lets x_t depend on history.
max_i sum x_ti - sum X_t, the actual deficit, as a random variable.
Full information setting where the whole x_t is observed; exponential weights with actual rewards.
